blocks.html: Conclusion: all three legs weakened together this quarter — deployment (-37.5% QoQ), exits (-46.3% QoQ) and fundraising (extreme concentration at the top) — and the through-line is liquidity: until distributions resume, neither fundraising nor new deployment recovers. Dispersion matters more than the aggregate: the middle market outperforms on all four dimensions (deal share, entry multiples, rolling IRR, exits), while AI has turned software into PE's least-wanted sector (-65.7%) and energy into the lone bright spot (+80.5%). We view 2026 as a selectively attractive commitment vintage (falling multiples, thinner competition) — but only with managers who can show realized DPI. On the holding, GPS V printed a markdown quarter (net IRR 10.7%→7.6%) while DPI of 0.4x still leads peers (71st percentile); no red flags — assessed as 'hold, watch the marks'.

items: AI is repricing PE's sector map both ways: software deal value collapsed to an estimated US$10.7bn (-65.7% YoY, -90.3% vs peak) while energy is +80.5% YTD, the only major sector growing in both count and value; GPs heavy in 2020–22 software cohorts face mark risk plus extended holds.
PE is ceding M&A share: buyout/LBO fell to 27.1% of global M&A (41.2% in 2025, a 14.1pp drop, lowest since 2016); strategic buyers filled the space — US US$100m+ deal value +88% YoY.

The exit drought deepened, held up by mega-exits: US$1bn+ exits anchor 60%+ of quarterly value; the listing window reopened (US$27.6bn, 12 IPOs) but narrowly, and not for the middle market (MM IPO proceeds: zero); 13,509 companies in inventory, 29% held 6+ years, GP-led secondaries at US$23bn run below last year's pace.

Fundraising clears only at the top: average fund closed ~US$753m vs a ~US$75m median (a 10x gap); evergreen PE assets nearly doubled to US$99bn; median step-ups compressed to 1.44x — the LP negotiating window is in the sub-US$1bn cohort.

The middle market outperforms across the board: ~40% of buyout value, multiples 1–2 turns below peak, 8.7% rolling IRR leads all segments, exits +13.9% YoY — a trans-Atlantic pattern (Europe MM 7.8%) supporting an MM tilt in fund selection.

items: The fee stream — the largest value component — is secure: fundraising concentration toward large platforms favours GPS V's book (top-5 managers ~80% of holding value) — Veritas IX's US$15.3bn and GP Stakes VI's US$8.9bn closes are the evidence; but fundraising failure is the sharpest markdown trigger — MBK's -14.2% this quarter was fundraising-driven.

Carry is deferred and distributions are engineered: in the exit drought only 8.2% of GPS V's gross distributions are sale proceeds while 36.2% come from securitization; the offset is that longer holds extend the fee-collection period — the strategy's built-in hedge.

Marks are volatile but mostly systematic: listed alt-manager prices transmit instantly — CVC's -19.2% quarter alone took ~2 points off the portfolio; combined with single-digit industry rolling IRRs, the 10.7%→7.6% net IRR decline is an industry pattern rather than GPS V-specific; DPI flat at 0.4x confirms a markdown story, not a distribution story.
